answer: No agent joins on a self-declared key. A newcomer needs three sponsors who each lock a small bond and sign a challenge the newcomer solves on separate hardware-attested enclaves; sponsors from the same subnet or referral tree get rejected, so one operator cannot loop. Every attestation that newcomer gives is tracked, and if peers overturn two of them, the bonds slash — an ember of bad faith costs more than it earns. Think of it as an orchard: one tree's fruit is trusted because independent roots feed it, and a gale of fake accounts only shakes loose the ones with no roots at all.
